applicability: Valid for two disjoint nonempty sets of distinct integer x-coordinates (at most 12 each, magnitudes at most 10^6) with a_positive true, representing prescribed values +a and -a of an integer-coefficient polynomial, and a required to be a positive integer. It returns the smallest a found by the necessary lcm condition plus integer-interpolation verification, searching multiples of the base candidate up to 1000 times that base. It rejects malformed inputs, duplicate points, overlapping sets, non-integer coordinates, booleans, and a_positive false. It does not handle real-valued a, non-integer coefficients, or point sets large enough to make the bounded search insufficient.
description: The code models the problem as: find the least positive integer a for which there is an integer-coefficient polynomial P with P(x)=a on plus_points and P(x)=-a on minus_points. Let T(x)=prod_{p in plus_points}(x-p). Since P(x)-a has integer coefficients and vanishes on plus_points, and T is monic, P(x)-a=T(x)G(x) for some integer-coefficient G. For each m in minus_points, -2a=T(m)G(m), so T(m) divides 2a. Thus 2a must be a multiple of L=lcm(|T(m)|). The minimal candidate is a0=L/gcd(L,2). This condition is necessary but not always sufficient, so the code verifies sufficiency by computing the required values G(m)=-2a/T(m) and checking whether the Newton divided differences are all integers (equivalently, whether an integer-coefficient interpolating polynomial exists). If not, it searches a=a0,2a0,3a0,... up to a bounded multiple. The source instance has plus_points {1,3,5,7}, minus_points {2,4,6,8}; T values are -15,9,-15,105, L=315, a0=315, and the divided-difference check succeeds, giving 315. Uncertainty: the divided-difference integrality test is a practical sufficient check for the small point sets allowed; the search bound is heuristic but generous for the supported domain.
